title: The Majestic Monolith
summary: DHH argues microservices fit organizations with thousands of developers, that small teams copying them are cargo culting, and that a deliberately integrated monolith let a dozen programmers ship a large product on six platforms.

assertions.quote: Every time you extract a collaboration between objects to a collaboration between systems, you’re accepting a world of hurt with a myriad of liabilities
M/SOA fits the organizational shape of very large corporations.
The patterns that make sense for organizations orders of magnitude larger than yours, are often the exact opposite ones that’ll make sense for you.
the only possible way to do so with a small team of ~12 programmers is do explicitly choose and commit to The Majestic Monolith

verdicts.note: Basecamp is a real existence proof, but a single company's experience does not show other approaches would have failed.

assertions.quote: It’s much easier to silo knowledge and responsibilities with a proliferation of smaller systems.

verdicts.note: Service ownership does concentrate knowledge by design; whether that is worse than monolith hotspots has not been measured.

assertions.quote: Integrate your systems until it’s impossible for one person to hold it all in their head.
